sequencing_note: recommended_order is a recommendation, not a constraint. H-01 first: it is the largest open blocker and the only finding that DEGRADED on re-measurement. H-03 second: a runner that can lose its own evidence makes every later measurement untrustworthy, so fixing it before the big builds means their results can be believed. H-04 third: the obligation manifest is the largest build and several other rows fold into it. H-02 sits late because it shrinks as the others land -- each new gate pays down part of the 39. H-09 is out of scope.
owner_semantics: `owner` is a WORK-LOCK, not an accountability field: it records which session HOLDS the row right now. 'unclaimed' means free to pick up. Claim a row before starting it, release it on commit ('unclaimed' or 'released @ <rev>'). Enforced by tests/hardening_status.py: an in_progress row may not be unclaimed, and a closed row may not still be held.
